correctness.rationale: The M-curvature definition is reduced exactly to a support-height maximization over translated polygon intersections. Dihedral symmetry leaves one half-edge of boundary difference vectors. For each of the two residue families, cyclic half-plane order gives two active-line regimes; the normalized height is quadratic on each regime because the denominator is constant. Explicit positive quadratic coefficients, matching switch values, and a stationary endpoint establish the global chamber maximum. Substitution yields the formulas, and the package checker reconstructs the original half-plane optimization independently.
risks: Finite numerical checks are diagnostic only; the universal statement rests on the analytic active-line proof.

Replacing a computer-only qualitative assertion by an exact analytic family formula supplies reproducible benchmarks, proves the ball-limit behavior, and analytically recovers the reported decagon extremality inside the families.
